content.title: Your Big Five snapshot
content.body: This preview highlights a few tendencies that may be more noticeable in your current responses. It is a starting point for reflection, not a fixed description of who you are.
bullets: Notice which patterns feel familiar in more than one context.
Keep in mind that habits can shift with roles, demands, and experience.
Use the full report to explore all five dimensions and their facets.

content.title: More detail is available in the full report
content.body: Your saved result can include dimension explanations, facet-level context, and practical reflection prompts. Access describes which report sections are available; it does not imply a more certain or more favorable result.

content.title: Your full Big Five report
content.intro: Read the report as a set of working hypotheses. Each dimension describes a continuum, and the pattern may appear differently across work, relationships, stress, and unfamiliar situations.
content.section_intro: Explore the five dimensions, the facets within them, and actions you may want to test. No single score defines your ability, character, or future.
content.closing: Keep what is useful, question what does not fit, and revisit the result alongside real examples from your life.

dimensions.title: Openness to Experience
dimensions.body: This dimension reflects how readily you may explore unfamiliar ideas, perspectives, aesthetics, and ways of doing things. Different contexts can call for curiosity, continuity, or a blend of both.

dimensions.title: Conscientiousness
dimensions.body: This dimension reflects how you may organize effort, follow plans, and manage responsibilities. Structure can support reliability, while flexibility can help when priorities change.

dimensions.title: Extraversion
dimensions.body: This dimension reflects how you may engage with social stimulation, activity, and outward expression. Quiet and energetic settings can each support different kinds of contribution.

dimensions.title: Agreeableness
dimensions.body: This dimension reflects how you may balance cooperation, trust, candor, and personal boundaries. Effective interaction can involve both consideration and clear disagreement.

dimensions.title: Emotional Sensitivity
dimensions.body: This dimension reflects how readily you may notice stress, threat, or emotional shifts. Sensitivity can provide early signals, while steadiness can support recovery; neither range determines resilience or worth.

content.intro: Facets add detail within each broad dimension. They may vary independently, so a broad range does not require every facet to look the same.

facets.label: Imagination
facets.description: Interest in possibilities, inner imagery, and alternative ways a situation could unfold.

facets.label: Aesthetic Sensitivity
facets.description: Attention to form, beauty, design, and sensory qualities.

facets.label: Emotional Awareness
facets.description: Attention to emotional nuance in yourself and in situations.

facets.label: Openness to Action
facets.description: Willingness to vary routines and try unfamiliar activities.

facets.label: Intellectual Exploration
facets.description: Enjoyment of ideas, questions, and conceptual complexity.

facets.label: Value Flexibility
facets.description: Readiness to examine assumptions and consider other value frameworks.

facets.label: Self-Efficacy
facets.description: Tendency to approach tasks with a sense of practical capability.

facets.label: Order
facets.description: Preference for organization, predictability, and clear arrangements.

facets.label: Dutifulness
facets.description: Attention to commitments, obligations, and agreed standards.

facets.label: Achievement Striving
facets.description: Energy directed toward goals, progress, and demanding standards.

facets.label: Self-Discipline
facets.description: Ability to continue effort when interest or energy fluctuates.

facets.label: Deliberation
facets.description: Tendency to consider consequences before acting.

facets.label: Warmth
facets.description: Ease in expressing friendliness and interpersonal interest.

facets.label: Sociability
facets.description: Preference for frequent contact and shared activity.

facets.label: Assertiveness
facets.description: Readiness to speak up, guide discussion, or take social initiative.

facets.label: Activity Level
facets.description: Preference for pace, movement, and a full schedule.

facets.label: Excitement Seeking
facets.description: Interest in stimulation, novelty, and energetic experiences.

facets.label: Positive Emotion
facets.description: Readiness to experience and express enthusiasm or enjoyment.

facets.label: Trust
facets.description: Initial willingness to expect fair or cooperative intent from others.

facets.label: Straightforwardness
facets.description: Preference for direct, sincere, and uncomplicated communication.

facets.label: Altruism
facets.description: Readiness to notice and respond to other people's needs.

facets.label: Cooperation
facets.description: Preference for reducing unnecessary conflict and finding workable agreement.

facets.label: Modesty
facets.description: Comfort with sharing credit and limiting self-promotion.

facets.label: Compassion
facets.description: Sensitivity to vulnerability, hardship, and emotional impact.

facets.label: Anxiety Sensitivity
facets.description: Readiness to detect uncertainty, risk, or possible problems.

facets.label: Irritability
facets.description: Readiness to experience frustration when needs or expectations are blocked.

facets.label: Sustained-Stress Depletion
facets.description: Tendency, under sustained pressure, to become drained, fatigued, or short of the energy needed to keep responding.

facets.label: Self-Consciousness
facets.description: Sensitivity to evaluation and how you may appear to others.

facets.label: Overload Exit Urge
facets.description: Tendency, when overloaded, to want to disconnect, withdraw, or change the situation immediately to reduce pressure.

facets.label: Stress Vulnerability
facets.description: Likelihood of feeling overloaded when demands accumulate.

content.intro: Ranges describe relative tendencies in this response set, not grades or ability levels.

ranges.label: Lower range
ranges.description: This tendency may be less prominent or may appear in narrower situations. Lower does not mean worse.

ranges.label: Middle range
ranges.description: You may shift between both sides of the dimension depending on context, role, or current demands.

ranges.label: Higher range
ranges.description: This tendency may appear more readily across situations. Higher does not mean better.

content.boundary: Small differences near a range boundary should not be treated as a sharp change in personality.

content.title: Turn the result into small experiments

actions.prompt: Choose one tendency and write down two recent situations where it helped and one where it created friction.
Try a low-risk behavior from the other side of the dimension and observe what changes.
Adjust one cue, routine, or boundary so the behavior you want is easier to repeat.
Revisit the experiment after a week and keep only what was useful in that context.

content.boundary: These are reflection ideas, not treatment, performance, or career prescriptions.

workplace.title: At work
workplace.body: Your tendencies may shape how you plan, communicate, respond to change, and manage stimulation. Role expectations and team norms can strengthen or soften the pattern.
workplace.prompt: Which working conditions help you contribute consistently, and which require deliberate adjustment?

relationships.title: In relationships
relationships.body: The same tendency may be helpful in one interaction and difficult in another. Consider communication habits, boundaries, repair, and the other person's context rather than ranking one style above another.
relationships.prompt: What helps you stay clear and considerate when your preferences differ?

content.boundary: This content does not predict job performance, determine employment decisions, rate relationship quality, or guarantee outcomes.
